evals.prompt: open an interactive claude TUI inside MXC on C:\repos\scratch
evals.expected_output: Does not run tui through a captured shell tool; opens a terminal tab if such a tool exists, otherwise prints the exact `pwsh -NoProfile -File <resolved mxc.ps1> tui --workspace C:\repos\scratch` command; states the session runs as a separate agent account with no fs/net policy and no host ~/.claude, and that /login is needed unless a token env var is set

evals.prompt: the sandboxed claude TUI in MXC just prints Access is denied and exits
evals.expected_output: Explains the IsolationSession agent account cannot read the host user's profile, checks the workspace is outside C:\Users\<user> (e.g. under C:\repos), and confirms the CLI was staged to %ProgramData%\mxc-sandbox\bin

evals.prompt: I want an interactive MXC claude session but with network blocked
evals.expected_output: States IsolationSession cannot restrict networking and Windows MXC offers a PTY only via IsolationSession, so interactive plus network policy is not possible; offers mxc-run with --deny-net for headless instead

evals.prompt: run claude -p 'hello' in the MXC sandbox
evals.expected_output: Should NOT trigger mxc-interactive: a headless -p prompt belongs to mxc-run
